rules.title: NJ LAD: no denial of rental based on lawful source of income (e.g., Section 8 voucher)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not deny a rental to a person based solely on the person's lawful source of income or lawful source of rent payment, including a Section 8 HUD voucher. The brochure describes the LAD as prohibiting housing discrimination based on source of lawful income or lawful source of rent or mortgage payment.
rules.citation: NJ Law Against Discrimination (LAD), as summarized in NJ Division on Civil Rights brochure, rev. ep. 06.18.15 (Q&A 2); specific statutory section not stated in this source
rules.quoted_span:
a landlord cannot deny the
lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to
rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful
income.
rules.exemptions: Per the brochure's LAD exceptions: rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit as a residence; rental of a room or rooms by the owner/occupant of an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; preference for persons of the same religion by a religious organization (not clearly relevant to source of income); the familial-status exemption for housing for older persons does not bear on this rule. The brochure does not say whether each exception applies to the source-of-income prohibition specifically.
rules.interaction: Part of the broader LAD anti-discrimination framework; the brochure does not address interaction with other NJ or local screening rules.

warnings: Source is a 2015-revised Division on Civil Rights brochure (rev. ep. 06.18.15), a secondary summary; the current statute was not verified and there is no statutory section citation for the source-of-income provision. Status 'in_force' is inferred from the brochure's present-tense description and needs human verification.
No effective or enactment dates appear in the text, so all lifecycle dates and effective_date are null. The retrieval date was not used as a law date.

The room-rental exemption for owner-occupied one-family dwellings applies only when renting a room or rooms; the coverage predicate cannot capture whether a room (not the whole unit) is being rented, so it approximates this with is_single_family and owner_occupied. Review needed.
The service/guide dog extra-fee prohibition and other disability, familial-status and discrimination provisions fall outside the six supplied categories, so no rules were drafted for them.

No rent increase limits, just cause eviction, security deposit, application screening fee, or algorithmic rent-setting requirements appear in this chunk. The NJ FAIR Act (NJ-ALG-01) is not supported by this source, so no fixture alias was assigned.
The source states that the Division does not handle ordinary landlord-tenant disputes such as evictions.
Draft only: an administrator must review legal meaning, exemptions, dates and interactions before import.
